sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Expatriate Worker Cross-Border Money Transmission Service

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France-United States Double Taxation Avoiding Protocol
European Union Treaties (TFEU and derived regulations on establishment and payments)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier, Articles L.561-1 to L.561-59 and R.561-1 et seq.; Code de commerce, Article L.561-45 as implemented by R.561-45 and the Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE); LOI n° 2016-1691 of 1 December 2016 (Sapin II); EU Directive 2015/849 (AMLD4) and Directive 2018/843 (AMLD5) as transposed by French law.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the ultimate beneficial owner's passport
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National identity and passport authority of the UBO's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / official company extract of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each manager and UBO (utility bill or municipal tax certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local utility provider or municipal authority of the holder's residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter for each shareholder and manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Shareholder's or manager's home-country financial institution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Attestation de dépôt de fonds (capital deposit certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: French credit institution or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, shareholders, managers, and senior officers against the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, OFAC SDN list, and French national freezing measures administered by the Direction générale du Trésor. Mandatory identification and enhanced due diligence of Politically Exposed Persons as defined by CSSF/ACPR regulatory guidance and Code monétaire et financier Articles L.561-10 et R.561-10; enhanced measures apply when the client or UBO is resident in a high-risk third country identified by FATF.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) via the Guichet Unique operated by INPI (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be expressed in French or in Latin characters; any non-French name must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet. The name must not violate the Toubon Law requirements for mandatory French-language public communications and may be refused if it creates confusion with an existing protected denomination. A precise phonetic uniqueness review is applied against the RNE and EU trademarks.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed name, the applicant may submit a formal administrative objection within one month of the notice through the Guichet Unique, attaching evidence of either prior use, trademark registration, or absence of confusion. If the registry confirms the rejection, an appeal may be lodged with the competent administrative court (Tribunal administratif) within two months of notification of the confirmation. A request for expedited treatment must be included in the filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For general commercial SARL formation, a French domiciliation address provided by an authorized domiciliation company is permissible and may serve as the registered office. However, for an ISIC 6619 cross-border remittance agent requiring an ACPR 'établissement de paiement' license, a mere virtual office is not sufficient; the licensed entity must maintain a physical operational office in France where management, AML/CFT compliance functions, and records are actually located. A virtual office may complement, but never replace, the required substantive presence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: approximately 70% cumulative likelihood of an unannounced on-site inspection by the ACPR or the Bank of France within the first twelve months of obtaining the payment institution license, based on prevailing supervisory intensity for high-risk money transmission firms.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: INPI Guichet Unique SARL incorporation registration fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Mandatory publication of legal notice of incorporation (avis de constitution) in an authorized legal gazette

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Approved domiciliation company or commercial office provider

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notary or attorney fee for drafting statuts, corporate governance documents, and conducting cross-border due diligence
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark and professional tariff schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation, notarization, and apostille of foreign corporate and personal documents
Bank attestation de dépôt de fonds (blocked capital certificate) issued after deposit of share capital
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French credit institution or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Title III, Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (SARL), supplemented by Articles R.223-1 to R.223-30; payment service licensing under the Code monétaire et financier (CMF), Book V, Title II.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registry of the Commercial Court) acting through the INPI single-business formalities portal (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Dossier d'immatriculation au RCS including the articles of association (statuts) and the standardized legal entity registration form (Formulaire M0).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: SARL has no statutory minimum capital; the articles may fix a nominal capital of at least EUR 1. All cash contributions must be deposited into a blocked account with a French credit institution or a notary, and the deposit certificate is released only upon RCS registration. For the ACPR payment institution authorization, higher own funds may be required under CMF Article L.522-11.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: The subscribers form a Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL) and approve the articles of association. RESOLVED: Each subscriber irrevocably subscribes to the number of shares set beside his or her name, acknowledging that the full amount of contributions has been deposited or will be paid to the company's blocked account. RESOLVED: The registered office is established at the address stated in the articles and may be relocated by ordinary decision. RESOLVED: Mr./Ms. X is appointed manager, and Mr./Ms. Y is appointed compliance officer, each with authority conferred by the articles. RESOLVED: This resolution takes effect immediately for filing with the Registry; all necessary filings and publications are authorized.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name verification and Articles of Association drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI / Infogreffe (RCS name and trademark search); optional notary for draft
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform an online conflict search against the French RCS database and the INPI trade register to ensure the proposed trade name is not identical or confusingly similar. Draft the articles (statuts) in French, including corporate identity, share capital, contributed property, share form, governance/manager clauses, and the exact registered office address. Have counsel review and initial the draft before formal execution.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of all shareholders and managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name conflict is identified, propose one or more alternative names and resubmit the search; trademark oppositions are resolved by INPI cancellation or coexistence agreement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital subscription and deposit in a blocked account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Each shareholder must fully subscribe for the capital indicated in the articles. Transfer the cash portion of the capital contribution to a temporary blocked account opened by the founders with a French credit institution or into a notarial escrow account. Obtain the attestation de dépôt de fonds and a list of subscribers with allocated shares.
required_dossiers: Identity documents and residence proof of subscribers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If discrepancies appear in the attestation, have the bank reissue a corrected certificate; if capital is delayed, submit a bank transaction record and obtain an amended deposit receipt.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of legal notice in a legal announcements journal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) approved in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and submit a notice of incorporation for publication in a JAL permitted for commercial companies. The notice must mention the corporate name, form SARL, capital amount, address, manager, and the registry where the company will be registered. Obtain the justificatif de parution within one day.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the journal issues a defective voucher, immediately request a corrected publication and submit the revised voucher to the registry; if publication is delayed, contact the journal's legal advertising department.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Constitutional shareholders meeting and adoption of the First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: All shareholders, manager(s), and notary if the articles require notarial form
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene and hold the constitutive shareholders meeting in accordance with the articles. Adopt the First Board Resolution confirming the authorized share subscription, the amount of contributed capital, the adoption of the registered office address, and the appointment of the first manager(s) and any compliance officer. Record attendance and sign the minutes in the presence of all members.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a shareholder is not physically present, execute a proxy or postal circular resolution; if any formal shortcoming is noted, adopt a corrective resolution or secure post-meeting ratification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing the incorporation dossier with the RCS via INPI
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI formalities portal (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), with filing to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the official portal and complete the legal entity registration form (Guichet unique). Upload the executed statutes, first resolution, attestation de dépôt de fonds, proof of JAL publication, and the form M0 data sheet. Pay the filing fee online and submit. Track the receipt and later the RCS extract (extrait Kbis).
required_dossiers: Déclaration de non-condamnation of the manager
Power of attorney if filed by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry raises a query, respond online within 15 days by submitting the correction or missing document; avoid rejection by resubmitting the corrected dossier and paying any additional fee only if expressly required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, statistical and social registration (SIREN, SIRET, VAT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INSEE and URSSAF via the automatic interface; tax registration via Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the RCS registration is complete, the INPI portal automatically transmits data to INSEE and tax authorities. Confirm that the SIREN/SIRET numbers, APE/NAF code (6619), and VAT number are activated. For cross-border remittance operations, request the correct VAT treatment from the tax office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIREN is not active within 48 hours, use the online complaint mechanism at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr or contact the local INSEE office; if the APE code is incorrect, file a rectification request through INSEE.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Premises compliance, fire safety and occupational health clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Mairie / Prefecture, Commission de Sécurité, and DREETS labor inspectorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a self-inspection of the registered office and any client-facing or processing premises to verify fire safety, electrical installations, emergency exits, accessibility for disabled persons, and compliance with Code du travail minimum conditions. Engage a certified safety officer for a control visit and obtain a fire safety certificate; file with the local mayor if the premises is open to the public.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an inspection report identifies defects, prepare an action plan and obtain a reinspection; apply for derogation or temporary occupancy while remediation works are carried out.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment institution license application (agrément PSP) with ACPR
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) – Banque de France
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the complete application package for the license to operate a payment institution providing cross-border remittance services. Submit the program of activities, internal AML/CFT policies, outsourcing arrangements, governance and internal control mechanisms, initial own-funds evidence, and the list of payment transaction supervisors. Follow ACPR's case-management system and maintain continuous dialogue during the review period.
required_dossiers: Program of activity and business plan
Own funds and prudential capital evidence
Operational security and IT risk policy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ACPR requests additional information, submit the supplemental document within the specified time (usually one month). For refusal, the applicant may reapply after correction or file an administrative appeal within two months of notification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) for payment-service authorization; Direction Départementale de l'Emploi, du Travail et des Solidarités (DDETS) for workplace health and safety.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Payment Institution Authorization (Agrément de prestataire de services de paiement) under Code monétaire et financier, Articles L.522-1 et seq.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition écologique / DREAL (Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – office-based service activity not listed in the French environmental authorization regime; no full EIA required, but premises exceeding 1,000 m² may require simplified energy and waste compliance registration.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or significant VOC emissions. Must comply with Code de l'environnement rules on DEEE (electronic waste), waste separation, and building energy performance (décret tertiaire).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the local Commission de sécurité, structural load assessment for IT/file rooms, compliance with Code du travail general obligations (ventilation, lighting, emergency exits), and accessibility for disabled persons (ERP rules).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), Ministry of Economy and Finance; professional portal: impots.gouv.fr; company registration via Guichet Unique at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; VAT/TIN allocation by DGFiP (Service des Impôts des Entreprises, SIE) with cross-border non-resident desk at SIEE (Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères, Noisy-le-Grand).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: File SARL incorporation (statuts, capital deposit certificate, director consent) at the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce through Guichet Unique; obtain SIREN (9-digit), SIRET (14-digit), APE/NAF code 6619Z and Kbis extract. Step 2: Submit form 3517-SD (regular tax regime election) via the same Guichet; DGFiP assigns the intra-Community VAT number in the format FR + 11 characters and opens the SIE-based taxpayer file. Step 3: Open the DGFiP Espace Professionnel for electronic filing of CA3/Ca12 VAT returns and IS (form 2065-SD and annexes). Step 4: For foreign non-established parties, register through SIEE and appoint a French tax representative if inside EU rules require; however, the FR_SARL is a resident French entity, so ordinary SIE registration applies. Step 5: Obtain the ACPR authorisation/registration as a payment service provider or as a registered agent of an authorised PSP (money transmission is a regulated activity), and annex the authorisation reference to the tax file.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation – the SARL defaults to Impôt sur les Sociétés (IS) on worldwide profits under Article 206-1 CGI regardless of non-resident ownership: standard 25% rate; reduced 15% on the first €42,500 of profit for SMEs with turnover under €10m and ≥75% individual ownership. France is a unitary national system with no sub-federal income tax; the remittance activity is resident in France by place of effective management (Article 209 CGI). Tax_Exempt_Zone: not applicable to mainland France; overseas DOM/TOM special zones are out of scope. Pass-through treatment is not automatic and requires the 5-year statutory election described below.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box; the relevant French statutory elections are: (1) Article 239 bis AA CGI – small SARLs (≤5 individual partners, qualifying industrial/commercial/artisanal/liberal activities) may elect pass-through taxation (régime des sociétés de personnes) for up to 5 years; revocation triggers immediate IS entry with reserve recapture. (2) Article 260 C CGI – option to tax (option pour l'imposition à la TVA) the otherwise VAT-exempt financial transactions, permitting recovery of input VAT on remittance operational costs where the agency is in a net input-VAT position. (3) Article 239 quater CGI – defunct 5-year start-up option for IR on newly formed SARLs. (4) No hybrid-mismatch election exists under French CFC rules; the EU ATAD/Pillar Two (15% minimum top-up under Directive EU/2022/2523) binds only groups with consolidated revenue exceeding €750m, which is inapplicable to this micro-remittance SARL. (5) If the SARL is held at ≥95% by a French PE, the parent may elect tax consolidation (intégration fiscale) under Article 223 A CGI.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: TVA – Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (French VAT under CGI Articles 256–289, transposing EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC). Cross-border remittance fees (money transmission, SWIFT fees, cash-pickup settlement, payment clearing) are VAT-exempt under Article 261 C 1° a) CGI as transactions concerning payments, transfers, deposits and debt claims; the exemption is without right to input VAT deduction unless the Article 260 C CGI option is exercised.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Franchise en base de TVA thresholds (Article 293 B CGI, adjusted by Loi de finances 2025): €110,000 for goods and €45,000 for services. A remittance agency performing exempt financial transactions must nevertheless be registered for VAT and file returns from its first euro of fees because the exemption under Article 261 C is a substantive exemption, not the small-business franchise; the entity is therefore subject to compulsory monthly CA3 filing of the régime réel normal irrespective of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Continuous transaction control (CTC) without real-time fiscal clearance: (1) From 1 September 2026, all French VAT-registered businesses must be able to receive B2B structured e-invoices; large and mid-sized enterprises (GE/ETI) must issue e-invoices through the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) or a certified Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire (PDP). (2) From 1 September 2027, small and micro enterprises (including this SARL) fall under the issuance obligation. (3) Mandatory formats: Factur-X (hybrid PDF/XML), UBL 2.1 and CII (EN 16931). (4) E-reporting: B2B transaction data, B2C sales data and payment status data must be transmitted to DGFiP electronically via PPF/PDP within two working days of the invoice or payment event; the French CTC is post-transaction with an extensive electronic audit trail, not a pre-clearance digital stamping API. (5) VAT-exempt remittance fee invoices must still be issued electronically and mention the exemption reference 'TVA non applicable – Article 261 C du CGI'.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The remittance service is not a zero-rated goods export; French VAT treatment is achieved by territoriality and exemption: (i) B2B fees invoiced to foreign established counterparties are outside the scope of French VAT under the place-of-supply rule of Article 259-1 CGI (service deemed performed at the recipient's establishment), resulting in 0% French VAT where the counterparty is outside France; (ii) B2C cross-border money-transfer fees are VAT-exempt (not zero-rated) under Article 261 C 1° a) CGI; (iii) any incidental physical export of tangible goods (e.g., POS hardware, cash logistics equipment to a non-EU branch) qualifies for 0% VAT under Article 262-I CGI provided the goods leave the EU within 90 days of dispatch when the exporter does not arrange transport; proof documents must be retained for 6 years.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: DAU – Document Administratif Unique electronic export declaration (DELTA-X / PVI system) where goods are physically exported
Bill of Lading (connaissement) or Airway Bill (lettre de transport aérien) evidencing outbound EU movement
Inward Remittance Certificate (attestation de rapatriement de devises) – bank confirmation that export proceeds were credited to the SARL's French bank account
Kbis extract and foreign customer's TIN/VAT registration certificate to support B2B place-of-supply status
Executed remittance mandate or correspondent agreement with foreign banks/agents plus SWIFT MT103/MT202 messages evidencing the cross-border settlement flow
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP and DGDDI joint audit controls apply; the statutory reprise period (délai de reprise) is 3 years for VAT and IS (Article L169 LPF), extended to 6 years on concealed activity or fraudulent manoeuvres (Article L176 LPF). Reassessed VAT and export-connected clawbacks carry 0.20% monthly late interest (Article 1727 CGI); bad-faith inaccuracies attract a 40% penalty, 80% for abusive/artificial arrangements or active concealment (Article 1729 CGI); e-invoicing and e-reporting failure is fined €15 per invoice and €250 per transaction (Article 1737 CGI). Criminal liability: tax fraud (fraude fiscale) carries a €500,000 fine and 5 years imprisonment, increased to €3m and 7 years for organised-gang fraud (Article 1741 CGI). Retrospective clawback of input VAT (reverse-charge at 20%) is imposed if the exemption or zero-rating claim is overturned; the SARL's manager and any signatory are jointly liable for the deficiency, interest and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (French central bank), in conjunction with the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) for licensing and prudential supervision of credit institutions and payment service providers, the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) for balance-of-payments reporting, and the European Central Bank (ECB) for common euro-area monetary policy. France applies fully the EU freedom of capital movements enshrined in Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible in France across both current and capital accounts. France maintains no exchange-control restrictions on current account transactions, foreign direct investment, or profit/dividend remittances. Capital movements are unrestricted within the EU and with most third countries, subject only to statistical balance-of-payments declarations to Banque de France. Profit remittance by a SARL to non-resident shareholders is lawful through an ordinary dividend distribution approved by shareholders, with the principal compliance hurdles being documentary (tax clearance status, annual-accounts approval in the shareholders' meeting, and dividend payment protocols) and treaty-based withholding tax liabilities rather than regulatory exchange controls. All settlements are freely denominated in euros or any counterpart currency at market-determined rates.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no statutory export-proceeds surrender rule and no mandatory conversion ratio for any category of exports, including remittance service revenues and trade-related receivables. Because the euro is the domestic legal tender and freely floatable, exporting entities may retain and manage foreign-currency proceeds offshore without conversion obligation. However, cross-border cash or bearer instruments in excess of EUR 10,000 must be declared at French customs, and all resident payment institutions must submit balance-of-payments reporting filings to Banque de France through the French Direct Investment and International Transactions Reporting System, including monthly corridor volume and counterpart country data.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. EU-domiciled Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) with a valid passport into France through the ACPR are operationally viable as segregated clearing counterparts for the SARL's remittance float, provided they maintain an ACPR-licensed e-money account and comply with safeguarding obligations under the PSD2. Offshore non-EU digital EMIs without a French or EU branch are rated Low: the ACPR and Banque de France require an EU-registered legal entity, a physical registered office, a local compliance officer, and internal audit arrangements in France; purely offshore EMIs cannot lawfully operate in the French remittance market.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: France imposes a mandatory due-diligence regime under Articles L.561-5 and L.561-6 of the Code Monétaire et Financier, which requires a meaningful identification interview for high-risk applicants. For a High-Risk, Special-License cross-border remittance SARL, at least one authorised signatory director or the designated registered agent must attend an in-person or ACPR-approved secure video-identity session before operational account activation. Purely remote opening is not permitted for a non-resident-majority-owned SARL with same-day money-transmission volumes; a local physical presence, authenticated civil-identity documents, and notarised powers of attorney for overseas signatories are mandatory first-principle requirements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: One or more directors or beneficial owners appears in PEP (Politically Exposed Person) sanctions-adjacent databases linked to the remittance network.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete PEP status explanation letter; certified Kbis extract dated within three months; beneficial-owner declaration under Article L.561-2-2; APD (Avis de Situation Débitrice) tax clearance certificate; notarised family and business relationship charts; explicit board resolution appointing a dedicated AML/CTF compliance officer (COSI) acceptable to the ACPR; list of target corridors and agent network agreements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO majority ownership is held through a non-EU shell holding company or discretionary trust.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled corporate registry extract of the ultimate parent; audited financial statements proving economic substance; notarised declaration of trust/beneficial ownership; source-of-wealth report for each material shareholder; complete organisational structure chart; bank reference letters from the home jurisdiction; evidence of real operational activity in the parent entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High velocity of same-day cash pickups to elevated-risk African or South-East Asian corridors creates a perceived money-laundering and fraud concentration risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transaction-flow diagram for each corridor; cash-pickup partner due-diligence files; customer identification and travel-rule compliance procedures; SAR escalation protocol and statistically calibrated thresholds; agent audit and trailing-stop framework; reconciliation and settlement-cycle documentation; independent compliance review engagement letter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wires referencing sanctioned states, parties, or partial-name fuzzy matches trigger automatic account freeze.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ongoing EU/UN/OFAC sanctions-screening output reports; a documented override committee procedure with an independent legal opinion; real-time names-matching algorithm test results; false-positive handling procedure; correspondent-bank standard terms acceptance; proof of a zero-tolerance policy for sanctioned jurisdictions and a formal indemnity in favour of the clearing bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity subscriptions into the SARL capital escrow account must originate from the ultimate investor's bank account and be transmitted by SWIFT MT103 with the EU/Banque de France balance-of-payments purpose code S302 (Direct Investment – Equity Capital). The receiving French bank requires the following verification bundle: apostilled and legalised subscription deed, updated Kbis extract, beneficial-owner declaration, board resolution approving the capital increase/call, source-of-funds certificate from the remitting bank, and the SARL's tax identification number imprinted in the wire narration. Funds must be credited to the segregated Capital Escrow Account, quarantined until the notary or registered agent confirms legal receipt and the Banque de France external direct investment declaration is filed where applicable.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound remittance disbursements clear through three rails: (A) intra-Eurozone beneficiary payments use SEPA Instant Credit Transfer or SEPA Core clearing at T+0/T+1; (B) non-euro international payments use SWIFT MT103 correspondent-bank settlement with strict purpose codes and dual-sided reconciliation; (C) high-volume African and South-East Asian cash-pickup corridors use licensed local payment aggregator sub-wallets and mobile-money API clearing pools (e.g. Orange Money, Wave, MTN MoMo, Wari) linked to the SARL's French operational account. Commercial Letters of Credit are uneconomic for remittance disbursements; however, documentary collection and standby LCs remain permissible for supplementary escrow or trade-backed settlement structures, subject to full compliance with EU sanctions and ACPR safeguarding rules.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla FX forwards (deliverable, typically up to 12-month tenors) for euro/USD, euro/GBP, and euro/CFA corridor exposures
OTC European-style FX options with premium payment and documented bona fide hedging intent
Cross-currency swaps (principal and interest exchanges) executed under ISDA/CSA with full collateralisation where the counterparty is a regulated French or EU bank
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for corridor currencies that are not freely deliverable onshore, provided the underlying remittance exposure is documented and the OTC counterparty is ACPR-authorised

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 3 months after the end of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties of 0.5% per month of delay on the tax amount due, capped at 25% of the tax, with risk of administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 3 months after the end of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties of 0.5% per month of delay on the tax amount due, capped at 25% of the tax, with risk of administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 3 months after the end of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of 100 EUR per month of delay, capped at 5,000 EUR, and potential administrative strike-off
Administrative fines up to 10,000 EUR and possible company strike-off proceedings

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent statutory audit if the company has an average of more than 20 employees, annual turnover exceeding 1,500,000 EUR, or total balance sheet exceeding 375,000 EUR
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (Plan Comptable Général - PCG) pursuant to the French Commercial Code

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual update and confirmation of ultimate beneficial owners, particularly required upon any shareholding transfers or significant ownership changes

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 100-300 USD for registered office or corporate agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 1,000-5,000 USD for statutory audit services depending on entity size

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) for fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2022
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate on first EUR 42,000 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs (turnover below EUR 10m and 25%+ owned by individuals for a continuous 2-year period); R&D tax credit (CIR) up to 30% of eligible research expenditure; innovation tax credit (CII) at 20% of eligible innovation expenses; the 5-year recognition horizon is a conservative DTA modelling convention, as the statutory carryforward of French tax losses is unlimited but capped annually at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the profit exceeding EUR 1,000,000

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (déclaration de résultat pour l'impôt sur les sociétés) with annual liasse fiscale 2053-SD to 2059-SD, filed electronically on the impots.gouv.fr PROFIL or EDI; the company must also transmit the Fichier des écritures comptables (FEC) within the electronic filing package
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual filing; four quarterly advance payments (each 25% of estimated current-year tax or previous-year tax if no current-year estimate) are due in March, June, September, and December, with the final balance settled at the annual filing date
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal year ending 31 December, the return is due by the second working day after 1 May. For a non-calendar fiscal year-end, the return is due within 60 days following the close of the financial year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company details: SIREN/SIRET, name of SARL, NAF/APE code corresponding to ISIC 6619 / NAICS 522390, address of registered office and principal establishment in France
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert French permanent establishment identifier; if no French PE, a foreign-owned SARL not operating through a PE is not required to file a French corporate income tax return for this activity

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit/loss before tax from the statutory financial statements
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only the French PE's accounting profit or loss attributable to the remittance business; head-office expenses are excluded unless deductible under treaty principles

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3C - Résultat fiscal après réintégrations et déductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit or deficit after applying statutory add-backs (e.g., non-deductible fines, 50% of entertainment expenses) and deductions (depreciation, tax-loss carryforward)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include transfer-pricing adjustments and disallowed payments if the foreign shareholder/agent is a related enterprise; attach TP documentation if the mandate applies

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses for the fiscal year available for later offset; French losses may be carried forward indefinitely but annual offset is capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the remaining taxable base
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-owned SARL may claim French losses against future French PE profits only if the loss carrying entity remains the same legal person in France and has continuous substance

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6A - Réductions d'impôt, crédits d'impôt et divers
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIR, CII, and other tax credits, netting against computed corporate income tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If claiming foreign tax credit treaty relief, attach form 2052-SD and the residence certificate of the ultimate foreign parent where applicable

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 10% surcharge on contested tax, plus late-payment interest of 0.20% per month; after formal request, the 10% late-filing penalty is raised to 40% in bad faith or 80% in fraudulent abuse; additionally a fixed penalty per missing box/annex may apply under Articles 1728 to 1729 CGI

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% French withholding tax on dividends paid by a French SARL to a non-resident corporate shareholder; 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive when a 10% or greater direct participation is held for at least two years; individual non-residents bear a 30% single flat rate (12.8% income tax + 17.2% social levies) with possible treaty reduction
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit Form 5001 (demande de restitution/convention fiscale) together with Form 5000 (certificat de résidence fiscale) to the payer's tax office before distribution; alternatively claim refund through the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères after withholding; the DTA relief is conditional on the ultimate beneficial owner establishing treaty residence, carrying no French PE during the relevant period, and satisfying the limitation-on-benefits or principal purpose test; processing generally takes 5 to 8 months
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 33.33% French withholding under Article 182 B for IP licence and technical service fees paid to a non-resident; treaty rates commonly 0%, 5% or 10% depending on the bilateral agreement. Interest: domestic arm's-length interest paid to a foreign lender is generally exempt from French withholding tax, provided the lender is not resident in a non-cooperative jurisdiction, where the rate becomes 75%, and anti-abuse recharacterisation under Article 57 can apply

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000: mandatory Local File/Master File is triggered when the French group or entity reaches annual tax-exclusive turnover exceeding EUR 400 million or holds controlled foreign entities meeting that asset threshold; an administrative guideline also expects simplified TP documentation from entities with annual turnover between EUR 50 million and EUR 400 million, especially in high-risk remittance flows; documentation may also be requested by the tax authority in audit even below threshold
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not administer a separate Economic Substances Regulations (ESR) code like common-law financial centres; however, doctrine and anti-abuse instruments impose substantive French activity demonstration for tax residence, permanent establishment creation, treaty entitlement (MLI Principal Purpose Test), and the 'abus de droit' doctrine. A remittance agency SARL must retain evidence of board meetings in France, employees, premises, settlement and clearing decisions, and arm's-length pricing of intra-group SWIFT/clearing fees

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of declared profits, hidden wire transfers, invoicing of fictitious remittance processing fees, or systematic underestimation of French PE revenue in cross-border money transmission
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 1741 CGI: 5 years' imprisonment and EUR 75,000 fine; where organized or aggravated circumstances apply, up to 7 years and EUR 100,000 fine. Additional 40% penalty for bad faith or 80% for abuse of law under Articles 1729 to 1730 CGI, plus late-payment interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who personally participated in or profited from fiscal evasion can be prosecuted for fraud; the court may impose a temporary or permanent ban from directing a commercial company, restriction to travel abroad (interdiction de sortie du territoire), confiscation of assets, and they can be held jointly and severally liable for the company's unpaid tax debts under Article L267 LPF where they committed irregularity

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a low-substance French SARL as a mere pass-through conduit for international remittances, interposing a tax-haven shell in the SWIFT chain without commercial justification
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The French tax administration may invoke abuse of law under Article L64 LPF; the company is liable for a re-determined tax increase, plus interest and penalties of 40% or 80% according to dominant intention or deliberate manoeuvring
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors liable in civil and criminal turf when the arrangement was designed, signed and executed for personal tax/AML evasion; court may order restitution, proportional financial sanction, and disqualification from managing a French company

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating cross-border remittance collection and SWIFT clearing without holding an ACPR licence for 'établissement de paiement' or agent registration under the French Monetary and Financial Code (CMF), including unregistered cash-transfer corridors
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unlawful provision of payment services is a delict under Article L521-2 CMF: imprisonment up to 3 years and fine up to EUR 375,000; may also trigger withdrawal of the SARL's registered commercial status in severe cases
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing partner (gérant) and effective managers are personally exposed to criminal sanctions for wilful supervision failure, civil liability for victims' funds, and no professional travel or account transfer allowances during the proceeding; court can impose a ban on managing a French company for up to 10 years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Incorrect margin on intra-group SWIFT transaction fees, cash pickup sustaining margins or excess license/clearing charges paid to a foreign parent, especially where the French SARL's net margin falls outside a comparable range for a limited-risk distributor
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment by French tax administration under Article 57 CGI; recapture of artificial profit into the French tax base, 40% penalty for deliberate misconduct or 80% for abuse; separate fixed fine of EUR 10,000 for failure to produce TP documentation when requested under Article L13 AA LPF
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held financially liable for added corporate tax and penalties when they signed related-party agreements without transfer pricing documentation, or knowingly set non-arm's-length rates stripping French profits; civil action may extend to seizure of personal assets

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: DTA Misuse and False Residence Certificate
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Representing the French remittance activity with a false TRC or orchestrating non-resident shareholder nominee layers to conceal the true owner and to misuse the parent-subsidiary directive 0% withholding
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Nullity of the tax relief claim; retroactive withholding levy at 25% or 30% with interest and sanctions; criminal indictment under Article 1741 CGI and Article 433-19 Code pénal for use of a false official document
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil is automatic for shell liability; court can order the managing partner to repay all mis-statutory distributions plus 80% penalty; travel ban applied when French treasury liability exceeds EUR 10,000
